stem: Which is an advantage of just-in-time (JIT) inventory control?

options.content: Bulk-buying discounts are easier to obtain
options.rationale: JIT uses small, frequent orders, so bulk discounts are lost.

options.content: Production continues even if suppliers are late

options.rationale: JIT needs less storage space.

options.content: A late delivery would halt production with no stock

options.rationale: Manufacturers use JIT widely.

options.rationale: Distance usually raises delivery costs.

stem: A brick works employs 15 workers who make 3,600 bricks a day. Calculate the labour productivity (bricks per worker per day).
The brick works (15 workers, 3,600 bricks a day) buys a new mixer. Now 13 workers make 3,900 bricks a day. Calculate the percentage increase in labour productivity, to one decimal place.
workedSolution:
1. Before: 3,600 ÷ 15 = 240 bricks per worker.
2. After: 3,900 ÷ 13 = 300 bricks per worker.
3. Increase = 60; percentage = 60 ÷ 240 × 100 = 25%.

stem: A tailoring business employs 6 machinists, each paid US\$145 a week. Together they make 1,160 shirts a week. Calculate the labour cost per shirt.
workedSolution:
1. Weekly wage bill = 6 × 145 = US\$870.
2. Labour cost per shirt = 870 ÷ 1,160 = US\$0.75.
hints: Find the total wage bill first.
